newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Oct 10.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Oct 10.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Parramatta league club is the only ARL-aligned club which has as yet to commit itself with the Optus Cup competition. Eleven other clubs, including the doubtful St George Dragons, have kept loyalty agreements to remain with the ARL-run competition. Page 24.

According to New South Wales and Sydney City coach Phil Gould, several Super League signed players are now re-thinking their initial decision, casting doubt over the stability of any new competition. Gould additionally rejected any possibility of a player exodus to the Super League ranks from ARL-signed players. Page 24.

The Ferozshah Kotla Cricket Ground at Delhi is not among the more attractive pitches or venues in world class cricket, but it should provide a wicket suited to bowlers - especially spinners - with little or no grass and plenty of cracks up the wicket.
Pag 24.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Newcastle will be willing to discuss any merger proposals with sister club Hunter Mariners, which possessed the Super League franchise for the region, according to Knights chief executive Ian Bonnette. This move is extraordinary in light of Newcastle resining for the ARL. Page 42.

Brilliant Epsom winner Filante may have another run in Melbourne before attacking the Cox Plate, Australia's weight-for-age championship. Filante was due to leave for Melbourne this morning and has been nominated for the Group 3 Coongy Handicap, over 2000 metres next Wednesday. Page 42.

The strongest team of Australian surfers to compete overseas has easily advanced through the preliminary heats at the World Surfing Games at Huntington Beach. The team includes Barton Lynch, Todd Prestage, Mick Barry, Jye Gofton, Darren Magee and Pete Hayes. Page 41.
THE AGE

Mark Bradtke proved last night that there is nothing more dangerous than a wounded tiger. Despite an early head clash with Brisbane's Bob Shelby, the star forward was on deck for the Tigers 111-93 win at Melbourne Park, stitching up a place in the Nationa Basketball League playoffs for the Tigers. Page B8.

Hawthorn forward Nick Holland brought football's trading market to a standstill yesterday by walking out on Hawthorn and refusing to be traded to Port Power. A disillusioned Holland said a feeling of betrayal has now permanently scarred his relationship wth the Hawks. Page B8.

Essendon has emerged as front-runner to secure the services of disgruntled Swans forward Anthony Rocca. It is believed that Rocca will nominate himself for a pre-season AFL draft in February, which will leave Sydney empty-handed unless they can trade him.Page B8.
HERALD SUN

Tribunal chairman Neil Busse has called on AFL clubs to break the code of silence that continues to shroud behind-the-play incidents in AFL football. Busse declared that club officials who are unwilling to lodge complaints against opposition offenders arehampering the administration of the game. Page 93.

The VRC and Harness Racing Victoria believe they are close to clinching a temporary solution to the mid-week TAB agency blackout. There could however be problems with Sky Channel over the introduction of a Channel 31, which would cover all race meets not exclusively covered by Sky. Page 92.

Trainer Kevin Prendergast has insisted that jockey Mick Kinane, who was victorious upon Vintage Crop in the 1993 Melbourne Cup, will ride European stayer Oscar Schindler if the horse comes to Australia for the November 5 meet. Page 92.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Australia's boxing world champion Kostya Tszyu will be introduced for the first time to the huge American and Mexican television audience before the clash between Julio Chavez and Joey Giamache. The opportunity could establish the Aussie as a marketable prsonality, worth millions in the US. Page 82.

Brisbane Cup winner Dupain is in grave danger of being balloted out of next week's Caulfield Cup, even if he beats the nagging hoof injury which has hampered any track work for the Cup chance. Page 82.

South Australian speedster Jason Gillespie is a surprise inclusion in the Australian team to play India in the one-off Test match starting today in Delhi. The 21-year-old has been kitted up in front of Victorian Damien Flemming. Page 84.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
